carried.group: T09-AUDIT-CLAIM-BYTES: the claim file's bytes are only parsed as JSON or hashed as read; nothing re-derives or compares them
carried.grounds: The claim file is written at lineage.py:179 as `json.dumps(doc, sort_keys=True) + "\n"`; the mutant drops only the trailing newline. Every reader parses it as JSON or hashes the bytes it read: claim() L147-153 (read_bytes -> json.loads; `_sha(data)` at L163, L168, L169 is the digest of the bytes on disk), continued_by L191 and lineage_account L346/L355 via _claimed_run (read_text -> json.loads, whitespace-insensitive). The claim file is outside the evidence manifest: run.py:294-304 evidence_manifest lists RUN.json, RUN.started.json, run/journals/*.jsonl, sessions/*.jsonl, preflight/* and, new in round 3, review-findings/*.json (L298-300); CONTINUED-BY*.json is none of these, and tests/v2/test_v21_kills3_T14a.py ManifestMembers (L136-170, NOT_MEMBERS holds CONTINUED-BY.json) pins it. The dict, not the file, goes into rec['continues']['claim'] (run.py:374); RUN.json is dumped with sort_keys (run.py:506) and its digest is of the canonical JSON (_content_sha, run.py:283-291). verify.py never opens a claim file (L84: lineage_account only). carried.group: T09-AUDIT-CLAIM-WORDING: connective punctuation of a refusal whose identifying elements (the flag, the 64-hex digest) are intact
carried.grounds: The conclusion holds; one consumer is misattributed in the carried text. CORRECTION: it says cli.py compares the named digest by equality; cli.py only forwards the flag (cli.py:67-68, :91 -> run.py:374), and the comparison is `supersede == _sha(data)` at lineage.py:163 inside claim() itself. Mutant: it drops the final ')' of the f-string at lineage.py:168 (same line): the refusal ends '... (an operator may name it: --supersede-claim <64 hex>' with the parenthesis unclosed. The flag and the digest are intact, and the digest is now the last token. The recovery instruction is held as a contract by tests/v2/test_v21_kills3_T09b.py:148-183 (ClaimRefusalText): it extracts the digest with `--supersede-claim\s+([0-9a-f]{64})(?![0-9a-f])` (L166), compares it with sha256 of the claim's bytes (L168) and supersedes with the extracted value (L169); the class docstring says 'the connecting words are not the contract'. The comparison that makes a copied digest work is `supersede == _sha(data)` (lineage.py:163): a copied trailing ')' would not match, so the mutant is the safer form for an operator copying the last token. The only producer of the text is lineage.py:166-168; its readers are run.py:373-376 (RunRefused(str(e)), recorded as rec['failure']['detail'][:2000] at run.py:498, of which verify.py:185 reads only the truthiness) and cli.py:92-93 (printed on stderr).

carried.group: T09-EQ-NOFOLLOW: O_NOFOLLOW beside O_CREAT|O_EXCL; O_EXCL already refuses a final-component symbolic link
carried.grounds: Equivalence holds. lineage.py:173-174 opens `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)`; the mutant's `getattr(os, "", 0)` is 0. O_NOFOLLOW governs only the final path component, and O_CREAT|O_EXCL already refuses a final component that exists, a symbolic link included, with EEXIST whatever it points at (POSIX open(); macOS open(2); Linux open(2): "symbolic links are not followed: if pathname is a symbolic link, then open() fails"; Linux build_open_flags ORs O_NOFOLLOW in for O_CREAT|O_EXCL itself - recalled, not readable on this host). Re-measured here on macOS / Python 3.14.7: dangling, to-file, to-dir, looping, regular-file and directory final components all give EEXIST (FileExistsError) with and without the flag; an intermediate symlinked directory is followed either way (the flag does not govern it). Where os has no O_NOFOLLOW (Windows) the original is already 0. The only handler is `except FileExistsError` (L175-177). Differential run at the snapshot (original module vs the mutant, claim lifecycle: refusal, supersede by digest, second generation, torn / non-object / run-not-a-string claims, dangling links, anchors written and read): identical on every observable, dangling links included.
